one_liner: Fundraiser for the National Gallery of Art who cultivates and solicits foundation and corporate donors, writes proposals, and project-manages exhibition fundraising and grants.
fit_summary: Your relationship-building, public-facing strengths and government-client consulting at IEM line up with the cultivation and stakeholder-management side of this role. However, the specialized experience requires documented fundraising or business development results, proposal preparation, donor solicitation AND managing a corporate prospect/donor portfolio. You qualify only if your IEM work (for example, business development, capture, or proposal writing) or volunteer fundraising can honestly show all three.
eligibility: Open to the public: U.S. citizens may apply, and no federal status is required.

You need one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-09 in fundraising or business development with documented results. It must include preparing proposals, soliciting new or existing donors, AND managing portfolio(s) of corporate prospects or donors to meet fundraising goals.
Alternatively, a Ph.D. or a qualifying combination of education and experience substitutes. Otherwise there is no education requirement.
You must pass a pre-employment background investigation, register for Selective Service if applicable, and be able to work some weekends and holidays.
strategy: Before applying, confirm your IEM role involved business development: writing or contributing to proposals for government contracts, pursuing new clients, or managing a client or pipeline portfolio. If it did, frame it as revenue generation with dollar figures and win rates.

Use the posting's exact language in your resume: 'prepared proposals,' 'solicited new and existing clients/donors,' and 'managed a portfolio of [X] prospects to achieve [goal].' HR cannot assume equivalence.

Add any volunteer fundraising, such as campaign finance calls, nonprofit galas, or political or community donor outreach, with month/year dates and hours per week. The posting explicitly credits volunteer work.
Keep the resume to two pages. List dates and hours per week for each role, and place the specialized-experience evidence in the first bullets of each job.
Preview the questionnaire, and answer 'expert' only where your resume shows proof. Overstating can remove you from consideration.
Apply between Oct 28 and Nov 11, 2026. Have a writing sample ready, such as a proposal excerpt or donor letter, because referred candidates may be asked for one.
resume_bullets: Prepared and submitted [number] proposals to [government/foundation/corporate] clients totaling $[amount], securing $[amount] in awards ([month/year–month/year], [hours]/week).
Managed a portfolio of [number] client/prospect relationships, developing outreach strategies and soliciting new and existing partners to reach a $[goal] revenue target; achieved [result].
Coordinated cross-functional teams of [roles] to deliver [project] on schedule, tracking milestones and stakeholder communications in [tool/CRM].
interview_questions: Walk us through a time you identified, cultivated, and closed a new funder or client. What was the result?
How would you build a relationship strategy for a foundation that has never given to the Gallery?
Describe how you managed competing deadlines across several proposals or grants.
How would you prepare a curator or executive for a solicitation meeting with a major sponsor?
watch_outs: The AND requirement (proposals, solicitation, and portfolio management) is strict. Consulting delivery work without business development or fundraising duties will likely be rated not qualified.
Some weekend and holiday work is required, and the commute is from Manassas to downtown DC (telework is available but the job is not remote).
The NF pay plan means the Gallery is not a standard GS agency, and the promotion potential tops out at NF-11.
The application window is only two weeks (Oct 28–Nov 11, 2026).
